note: Almost all of this lesson (11:13-1:00:35) is a listening drill on make-X / get-X verbs: Medi translates Amal's Arabic, so most rows are mode=listening. Ending/prefix misreads were ruled grammar (B1/B5/B10/B12/B18/D3/D4); only a different root (زعل vs زعج) stays vocab.

row.medi_said: This is it today. تسعة عشرين.
row.why: He said 29 for the date 19 (a different number = different word, tier 1); Amal said '19' and he took it at 06:42 تسعة عشر.

rulings.why: Real slip; tier 1 (wrong number, not a wrong form of the right one), Amal's bare '19' is a recast he took.

Duplicate of A1: her 07:12 تسعطاش تسعة fixes the month ستة -> تسعة again (he repeated it at 07:10); his 07:10 تسعش is already the spoken 19, and his 07:15 MSA تسعة عشر got no voiced signal (chat alone is not a correction, GR-19).

row.why: He stalled after أزرق on a word the engine wrote كمي (maybe كحلي 'navy'); Amal supplied غامق and he repeated it - she gave the word he lacked, so tier 0.

rulings.why: Real help from Amal mid-sentence, but كمي is not a clear wrong word (could be كحلي, a right word); tier 0 = she supplied it, low confidence.

row.medi_said: Why did you smile to a male or why did she smile?
row.right: why do you laugh / smile (بتضحك present)
row.why: He read the b- present بتضحك as past; Amal 'Is it did or do?' and he fixed at 15:58 'Why do you smile? Present tense'.

rulings.why: The fix is the b- = present rule (B1), so grammar, not vocab.

row.medi_said: He will not, he will not bore you.
row.amal_said: Very close. أزهقك، not يزهقك. أزهقك.
row.why: He read the I-prefix of أزهقك as the he-prefix; Amal 'أزهقك not يزهقك', 'I won't bore you'.

rulings.why: Real; the slip is the person prefix on the verb (B18), not a different word, so grammar.

row.medi_said: so don't be tired of me.
row.amal_said: That's ما تتعبي مني. ما تعبيني.
row.why: He read the make-X form تعبيني as get-X; Amal contrasted ما تتعبي مني vs ما تعبيني and he fixed to 'don't make me tired'.

rulings.why: make-X vs get-X is B12 grammar.

row.why: He read the ending on علي as عليه; Amal repeated علي, he fixed 'She laughed at me', she then said 'علي and عليه'.

rulings.why: Person ending on a preposition = D3.

row.why: He called past اتأسفوا present; Amal 'لأ, اتأسفوا not بيتأسفوا' and he fixed.

rulings.why: Past vs present recognition = B5 grammar.

row.medi_said: Oh, khirbat. Uh, she ruined the trip.
row.amal_said: No؟ ... That would be خربت. خربت.
row.why: He read get-X خِربت (got ruined) as make-X 'ruined'; first 'I ruined' at 39:31 (Amal 'Are you sure? I ruined?'), then 'she ruined' - 'No? That would be خرّبت'; he fixed at 40:14 'the trip was ruined'.

rulings.why: make-X vs get-X = B12; one row for the 39:31-39:47 run.

row.medi_said: uh, you guys don't, don't be annoyed.
row.why: He read زعل (sad) as annoyed (زعج, another root); Amal 'Annoyed?' and he fixed at 49:38 'don't be sad'.

rulings.why: Different lexical item (زعل vs زعج) = vocab tier 1.

row.why: He read make-X تزعجوه as get-X تنزعجوا; Amal named both forms; he reached 'don't be annoying to him' at 53:17.

rulings.why: make-X vs get-X = B12.

row.why: He read the object ending -ني as 'us'; Amal repeated زعلوني and he fixed 'They made me sad'.

rulings.why: Object ending on a verb = D4.

row.amal_said: صح، it made happy، بس is it past or present؟
row.why: He read b- present بيبسطني as past; Amal 'past or present?', he fixed 'it makes me happy'.
row.english: It makes me happy to come.

rulings.why: b- = present is B1.

row.medi_said: They had fun or they enjoyed?
row.amal_said: آآآ. Close بس that would be انبسطوا. انبسطوا
row.why: Her chat enbes6u is the command form (vs past enbasa6u she types at 1:02:22); he read it as 'they had fun', Amal 'Close but that would be enbasa6u'; he moved to 'you guys' but never to a command.

rulings.why: Real slip (Amal 'Close but'); the chat spelling enbes6u vs enbasa6u shows command vs past, so B10 rather than B5.
Duplicate of D5 (same 22:16 أزهقك moment); the full grammar B18 row is written under D5.

row.medi_said: Who was he mad with you-- at you? I don't... This doesn't make sense.
row.amal_said: What's ضايقك؟ ... So is it ضايق or it's ضايقة to be upset؟
row.wrong: who was he mad at you
row.why: He could not read make-X ضايقك (took it as 'be mad'); Amal prompted 'What's ضايقك? ... ضايق or تضايق to be upset?' until he said 'who made you upset' at 28:17.

rulings.why: Real; her prompts are about make-X vs get-X (ضايق vs تضايق), so B12 grammar rather than vocab.

row.medi_said: Uh, are you excited to a girl?
row.why: He read past تحمستِ as present 'are you excited'; Amal recast 'Did you get excited?' and he repeated it at 43:25.

rulings.why: Her English recast is a voiced fix of the tense he gave; he took it.

row.medi_said: She was happy. ... I enjoyed to it.
row.amal_said: No، انبسطت له. ... Just the verb. I got happy له. ... For، for him.
row.right: I got happy for him (انبسطت له)
row.why: Her 'No' answers 'I enjoyed to it': he misread له; she said 'For, for him' and he fixed at 50:53 'I got happy for him'. 'She was happy' alone was not wrong (her chat gives enbasa6etlo too).

rulings.why: Real slip on the ending of the preposition له (D3); the person was not the error.

Not an error: her own chat enbas6tu ma3o (1:01:44) is 'you (plural) had fun with him', so his 'you guys ... with him' matched; her 'Did you have fun with him?' only turned it into a question and he had already offered 'with him'.

row.medi_said: Did, uh, did you guys enjoy to me? ... I don't understand this one.
row.amal_said: Great that you got the [لي] part صح. They got-- they were happy for me.
row.why: Amal praised the لي part (engine wrote 'day part') and fixed the person: -u = they, not you guys (-tu); chat enbasa6uli; he took 'They were happy for me'.

rulings.why: Her fix is the past-tense person ending (B5), not the preposition, which she said he got right.

added.medi_said: So basat is I was happy.
added.why: He read make-X بسطه as get-X 'I was happy' (after 'So I am happy... No' at 32:21); Amal 'So بسطت first. I made.' and he fixed at 32:46 'I made him happy'.

challenges.why: Wrong label: 'you are tired of me' for تعبتني is the make-X vs get-X misreading (Amal: 'that's تعبت مني. تعبتني'), same as D6/D11 - grammar B12, not vocab tier 1.
Wrong bucket: his ma is right (B11 is ma vs la); the slip is the missing t- of the tet- prefix (matahammasi for ma tet7ammasi) - a form slip, possibly only S4 sound; audio check.
